title: Hokkaido in 6 Days | Sapporo, Jōzankei, Otaru, Furano and Biei (Winter)
subtitle: Winter: one night at Jōzankei Onsen, four in Sapporo, with day trips to Otaru and to Furano and Biei
summary: Six winter days in and out of New Chitose Airport: one night at Jōzankei Onsen and the rest in Sapporo, with the Otaru Canal, Hokkaido Shrine and the city's food, plus a day tour to Furano and Biei with no particular tour company named. The notes cover snowy roads, short daylight and transport delays. Shiraito Falls and the Jōzankei product hall are held as alternates.
destination: Sapporo, Jōzankei, Otaru, Furano and Biei, Japan

What changed and what was left out

The travelogue covers a mid-March trip; this template is marked as winter and adds reminders about snowy roads, short daylight and transport delays, while keeping the order of the travelogue's itinerary.
The travelogue's choice and prices for the day tour are not used; by the rules no company is named, so only the order of stops is listed, with a way to get there yourself.
The travelogue's Sapporo Tsunagu Yokochō (open only until March) and its Le Labo price reference are not used.

On day 5, the travelogue's order of Hokkaido Shrine and Maruyama Park is changed to go to the shrine first and then eat lunch, because daylight is short in winter and the shrine should be visited in daytime.
The travelogue browsed Sapporo Tōkyū Department Store, but its trading status could not be confirmed, so this template leaves it out.
Travelogue details

Lodging: the travelogue's author stayed at Yuraku Sōan in Jōzankei (1 night) and Keio Prelia Hotel Sapporo by the Sapporo Station north exit (4 nights), both the author's actual stays; room rates and location are in the travelogue.
Winter reminders

Snow and road conditions: from December to February central Sapporo has snow and ice, and the countryside is deeper. The paths and bridges at Jōzankei, Furano, Biei and Shirahige Falls are often icy, so walk slowly. In the mid-March travelogue the snow in town was already thin but the countryside still had snow, and Shiraito Falls and the suspension bridge were closed by it; deep winter will be worse than the travelogue.

Shoes: wear snow boots with non-slip soles or add ice cleats; do not wear ordinary sneakers. Security at Japanese airports is strict and boots must come off for the X-ray, so choose a pair that is easy to take off.
Clothing: a warm coat, thermal underwear, gloves, a hat and a scarf. It gets colder after dark, and the travelogue notes it stays very cold after the sun goes down.

Short daylight: around the winter solstice it is dark by about 16:00, so most sights need to be done early in the afternoon. Check Sapporo's sunrise and sunset times before you go and put outdoor sights in the daytime.

Transport delays: in heavy snow, JR Hokkaido, buses and flights at New Chitose Airport may be delayed or suspended. Do not pack the schedule too tight, leave a buffer for important reserved departures, and check JR Hokkaido and airline notices before you leave.
Daily transport is mainly JR and buses; the day tour on day 4 is a long ride, and winter roads may make it slower.
Between the airport and town (New Chitose Airport, CTS)

First choice is the JR Rapid Airport (快速エアポート): the airport station is on B1, follow the signs for "Domestic Terminal, JR Line". It takes as little as about 33 minutes to Sapporo Station (special rapid), about 37 minutes for the ordinary rapid and about 43 minutes for the section rapid; about 6 trains an hour from 9:00 to 16:00. You can tap a transit IC card straight through the gate without queuing at a ticket machine. Cars 1–3 and 5–6 are unreserved seating, and car 4 is reserved.
Fare: not listed on the official page and not in the travelogue; check the fare page of the JR Hokkaido website.
Some trains run through to Otaru, but not every one, so check the train's destination before boarding. Local trains marked "Local" do not go to Otaru.

Backup: an airport bus, for example the Hokuto Kotsu airport bus to Makomanai Station, where you can change to a Jōzankei bus, takes about 120 minutes in all; for ordinary airport buses to Sapporo, check the official site.
On day 6 the travelogue took the 11:19 JR Rapid Airport from Sapporo Station to the airport, about 38 minutes, arriving at 12:00.
Getting around Sapporo and Jōzankei

The smoothest way from Sapporo Station to Jōzankei is the Kappa Liner (かっぱライナー号): about 60 minutes, all seats reserved (no assigned seats), booked on the official site, boarding at Sapporo Station boarding point 27. The fare is ¥1,700 one way, ¥1,460 at the online booking discount; the travelogue paid ¥2,920 return. Booking opens about one month before the ride and closes at 17:00 the day before; the e-ticket is activated on your phone and shown to the driver, with no ticket to collect.

The 16:00 and 17:00 departures from Sapporo Station are autumn and winter only and run only as far as the Jōzankei garage; choose your boarding and alighting stops when you book. The travelogue's author chose to get off at Shiraito Falls stop, the closest to the hotel; you can also ride on to Jōzankei Onsen Higashi 2-chōme stop, right at the hotel door.

Two other routes (Jōzankei Tourism Association information from 2025/12): from Sapporo Station take the Namboku Line subway to Makomanai Station and change to a Jōzankei bus, about 70 minutes, no reservation needed, roughly every 30 minutes; Sapporo's bus terminal (Esta) is under renovation, and ordinary Jōzankei buses from the station front run only a few times in the morning, so the subway plus bus or the Kappa Liner is more practical.

The subway is very convenient in Sapporo: on the Namboku Line it takes about 3–5 minutes from Sapporo Station to Ōdōri and Susukino, and for Maruyama-kōen Station you change to the Tōzai Line at Ōdōri. Transit IC cards work throughout.
Reservations and tickets
Kappa Liner: reserve on the official site; the address is in the sources.
Otaru Aquarium: tickets can be bought online on the official site, and you show the QR code at the entrance.

Day tour: several travel agencies run this tour from Sapporo (Furano's Ningle Terrace, Biei, Shirahige Falls and Blue Pond illumination); before you go, compare the meeting points, whether lunch is included and the winter illumination period. The travelogue's author chose a plan leaving at 11:50 in the middle of the day and returned to Sapporo's Ōdōri Station around 21:00 that evening.

Doing it by public transport yourself: take the JR Hakodate Main Line from Sapporo Station to Asahikawa and change to the Furano Line to Furano, about 2–3 hours; from Furano to Biei you can take the JR Furano Line; Biei's Blue Pond and Shirahige Falls are far from the station, so in winter you mostly rely on taxis or a rental car. If you drive in winter, assess the risk of snowy roads yourself, and driving is not recommended if you are not used to snow. For times and fares, check the JR Hokkaido website.
Blue Pond illumination: only at night in winter, with dates and times that differ each year; check the Biei Town tourism association.
Entry and internet
Register on Visit Japan Web before you leave; immigration and customs share one QR code: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001 .

For the internet you can use a physical SIM card or an eSIM; an eSIM has to be activated somewhere with a connection, so it is best to set it up in Taiwan before you leave. The travelogue's author briefly lost signal only deep in the hills of Biei.
You can check in online and choose seats three days before your return flight, saving time in the airport queue; see the airline's website.
Pace of the trip
Days 1 and 6 include airport transfers and day 4 is a full day of transport for the day tour, so transport takes a larger share than the usual 30%. On day 4 the return to Sapporo is at about 21:00.
The Otaru Aquarium is open only until 16:00 in winter, so on day 3 visit the aquarium first, then the canal and Sakaimachi-dōri.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 6 days run
paragraphs: In and out of New Chitose Airport, with the first night at Jōzankei Onsen and the next four based at Sapporo Station's north exit. Otaru, Furano and Biei are all out-and-back from Sapporo in a day. This is a winter trip with short daylight and icy ground, so outdoor sights are kept to the daytime.

Day 1: land at New Chitose, take JR to Sapporo Station, then the reserved Kappa Liner from boarding point 27 to Jōzankei, check in at the onsen inn, and have an izakaya dinner on the hot-spring street.

Day 2: {@d2-02}, the Kappa Family Wishing Foot Bath and Jōzankei Gensen Park in the morning, with a bakery stop and Iwato Kannon Hall, then collect your luggage at noon and take the bus back to Sapporo to check in; in the evening {@d2-09}, Genghis Khan grilled lamb, Tanukikōji, and the night view from {@d2-12}.

Day 3: the train to Otaru, first {@d3-02} (it closes at 16:00 in winter), lunch at the Sanbanko café, then {@d3-04}, Sakaimachi-dōri and the {@d3-06}, and soup curry to take away for dinner back in Sapporo.

Day 4: after breakfast meet at Ōdōri Station exit 31 for the Furano and Biei day tour from Sapporo: {@d4-03}, the herb garden, Biei Station, the Biei Christmas Tree and Shirahige Falls, then {@d4-08} at dusk, back in Sapporo around 21:00.

Day 5: daylight is short in winter, so start at {@d5-01}, then milk ice cream and conveyor-belt seafood sushi in Maruyama, Daimaru Sapporo and the {@d5-05} in the afternoon, and wagyu yakiniku at night.
Day 6: JR to New Chitose Airport, souvenirs and food at the domestic terminal, then check in and depart at {@d6-02}.
Where to sleep: the first night at Yuraku Sōan at the entrance to Jōzankei's onsen street, then four nights from day 2 at Keio Prelia Hotel Sapporo by Sapporo Station's north exit.

Getting around: the JR Rapid Airport runs from the airport to Sapporo in about 33 to 43 minutes and takes a transit IC card; the Kappa Liner from Sapporo Station to Jōzankei takes about 60 minutes and every seat must be reserved; in Sapporo you mostly ride the subway. Heavy snow can delay JR, buses and flights, so leave a buffer for any fixed booking; the day tour on day 4 is a long drive and winter roads may slow it further. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants onsen, the Otaru canal, Furano and Biei in one winter trip. Wear non-slip snow boots and pack warm clothes; you get back to Sapporo around 21:00 on day 4, so save your energy for that day.

todos.note: Several operators run one; confirm the meeting point, the departure time, whether the Blue Pond illumination is included and the winter season dates

leg.note: By coach, about 1 hour 40 minutes from Sapporo to Furano, expressway and mountain road; the travelogue's tour was a small group of 6

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go

leg.note: By coach, about 20 minutes

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go

leg.note: By coach, about 2 hours 30 minutes, with a toilet stop at a roadside station around 20:00; winter roads and weather may cause delays

closingLeg.note: About 6 minutes by subway from Ōdōri Station to Sapporo Station, about 25 minutes including walking; most restaurants are closed by the time you return, so you can buy a late snack at a convenience store near the station

leg.note: Subway on the Namboku Line from Sapporo Station to Ōdōri, change to the Tōzai Line to Maruyama-kōen Station, about 20 minutes; from exit 3 it is about 15 minutes on foot through Maruyama Park, snowy and icy in winter

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go

leg.note: Beside the shrine approach; eating is not allowed inside the shrine, so finish at the tea house before going in or out

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go; recommended by the travelogue, with queues at peak times

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go

leg.note: Tōzai Line from Maruyama-kōen Station to Ōdōri, change to the Namboku Line to Sapporo Station, about 20 minutes, about 25 minutes including walking

events.notes: Check the building's opening hours before you go; the exterior is visible all day

leg.note: About 12 minutes on foot from the south exit of Sapporo Station; the road is slippery in winter

leg.note: About 10 minutes on foot from the red-brick building, in the next building over

leg.note: About 15 minutes on foot to Sapporo Station

closingLeg.note: About 10 minutes on foot back to the hotel by the north exit

events.title: New Chitose Airport domestic terminal: souvenirs and food (新千歳空港 国内線ターミナル)

place.address: 〒066-0012, 北海道千歳市, 美々987-22, 新千歳空港

events.notes: Check each shop's opening hours before you go; the 1st floor of the terminal has plenty of food and souvenirs

leg.note: JR Rapid Airport from Sapporo Station takes about 38–41 minutes to New Chitose Airport Station, about 55 minutes including walking and exiting; the travelogue's author took the 11:19 and arrived around 12:00

events.title: New Chitose Airport international terminal: check-in and departure

place.name: New Chitose Airport International Terminal
place.address: 北海道千歳市, 美々

leg.note: Walk from the domestic terminal to the international terminal; the travelogue warns that the farthest counters are an extra 165 metres' walk; security at Japanese airports is strict, and boots must come off for the X-ray

todos.text: Check in online and choose seats three days before your return flight
todos.note: Do it on the airline's website to save time in the airport queue
